sanskrit: nivāraya sutān dyūtāt pāṇḍavān mā druheti ca suhṛdāṃ hitakāmānāṃ bruvatāṃ tat tad eva ca
english: "Restrain your sons from the dice-game, and do not wrong the Pāṇḍavas"—so spoke your well-wishers, who sought your good, again and again.

sanskrit: na śuśrūṣasi yad vākyaṃ martyaḥ pathyam ivauṣadham tad eva tvām anuprāptaṃ vacanaṃ sādhu bhāṣitam
english: That counsel, well spoken, which you would not heed—as a sick man will not take the medicine that would heal him—has now overtaken you, fulfilled.

sanskrit: viduradroṇabhīṣmāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ hitaiṣiṇām akṛtvā vacanaṃ pathyaṃ kṣayaṃ gacchanti kauravāḥ
english: Having failed to follow the wholesome words of Vidura, Droṇa, and Bhīṣma, and of the other well-wishers, the Kauravas now go to their ruin.

sanskrit: tad etat samatikrāntaṃ pūrvam eva viśāṃ pate tasmān me śṛṇu tattvena yathā yuddham avartata
english: All this came to pass long ago, O lord of peoples; therefore hear from me, in its truth, how the battle unfolded.

sanskrit: madhyāhne sumahāraudraḥ saṃgrāmaḥ samapadyata lokakṣayakaro rājaṃs tan me nigadataḥ śṛṇu
english: At midday a most terrible combat arose, one that wrought the destruction of the world, O king; hear of it as I recount it.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi sainyāni dharmaputrasya śāsanāt saṃrabdhāny abhyadhāvanta bhīṣmam eva jighāṃsayā
english: Then all the armies, at the command of the son of Dharma, rushed forward in fury, eager to slay Bhīṣma himself.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ yuktānīkā mahārāja bhīṣmam eva samabhyayuḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin and Sātyaki, that great chariot-warrior, with their ranks marshalled, O great king, advanced against Bhīṣma alone.

sanskrit: arjuno draupadeyāś ca cekitānaś ca saṃyuge duryodhanasamādiṣṭān rājñaḥ sarvān samabhyayuḥ
english: Arjuna and the sons of Draupadī and Cekitāna, in the battle, fell upon all the kings whom Duryodhana had appointed.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tathā vīro haiḍimbaś ca mahārathaḥ bhīmasenaś ca saṃkruddhas te 'bhyadhāvanta kauravān
english: The hero Abhimanyu, and the son of Hiḍimbā, that great chariot-warrior, and Bhīmasena, full of wrath—these rushed against the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tridhābhūtair avadhyanta pāṇḍavaiḥ kauravā yudhi tathaiva kaurave rājann avadhyanta pare raṇe
english: Divided into three, the Pāṇḍavas struck down the Kauravas in the fight; and likewise, O king, on the Kaurava side the foes were struck down in the battle.

sanskrit: droṇas tu rathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ somakān sṛñjayaiḥ saha abhyadravata saṃkruddhaḥ preṣayiṣyan yamakṣayam
english: But Droṇa, foremost of chariot-warriors, full of wrath, charged the Somakas together with the Sṛñjayas, meaning to send them to the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tatrākrando mahān āsīt sṛñjayānāṃ mahātmanām vadhyatāṃ samare rājan bhāradvājena dhanvinā
english: There arose a great wailing among the high-souled Sṛñjayas, O king, as they were slain in the battle by the archer, the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: droṇena nihatās tatra kṣatriyā bahavo raṇe viveṣṭantaḥ sma dṛśyante vyādhikliṣṭā narā iva
english: Many warriors, smitten there by Droṇa in the fight, were seen writhing upon the ground like men tormented by disease.

sanskrit: kūjatāṃ krandatāṃ caiva stanatāṃ caiva saṃyuge aniśaṃ śrūyate śabdaḥ kṣutkṛśānāṃ nṛṇām iva
english: Of those moaning and wailing and groaning in the battle, an unceasing din was heard, like that of men wasted by hunger.

sanskrit: tathaiva kauraveyāṇāṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ cakāra kadanaṃ ghoraṃ kruddhaḥ kāla ivāparaḥ
english: In the same way the mighty Bhīmasena wrought a terrible slaughter among the Kauravas, raging like a second Death.

sanskrit: vadhyatāṃ tatra sainyānām anyonyena mahāraṇe prāvartata nadī ghorā rudhiraughapravāhinī
english: As the armies slew one another in that great combat, a dreadful river began to flow, streaming with floods of blood.

sanskrit: sa saṃgrāmo mahārāja ghorarūpo 'bhavan mahān kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yamarāṣṭravivardhanaḥ
english: That battle, O great king, of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas grew vast and dreadful in form, swelling the kingdom of Yama.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo raṇe kruddho rabhasaś ca viśeṣataḥ gajānīkaṃ samāsādya preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: Then Bhīma, wrathful in the fight and especially fierce, fell upon the host of elephants and dispatched them to their death.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata bhīmena nārācābhihatā gajāḥ petuḥ seduś ca neduś ca diśaś ca paribabhramuḥ
english: There, O descendant of Bharata, the elephants struck by Bhīma's iron shafts fell, and sank down, and trumpeted, and wandered through the quarters.

sanskrit: chinnahastā mahānāgāś chinnapādāś ca māriṣa krauñcavad vyanadan bhītāḥ pṛthivīm adhiśiśyire
english: The great elephants, their trunks lopped off and their feet severed, O venerable one, cried out in terror like curlews and lay down upon the earth.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca hayānīkam abhidrutau te hayāḥ kāñcanāpīḍā rukmabhāṇḍaparicchadāḥ vadhyamānā vyadṛśyanta śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Nakula and Sahadeva charged the host of cavalry; and those horses, decked with golden frontlets and trappings of gold, were seen being slain by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: patadbhiś ca hayai rājan samāstīryata medinī nirjihvaiś ca śvasadbhiś ca kūjadbhiś ca gatāsubhiḥ hayair babhau naraśreṣṭha nānārūpadharair dharā
english: With the falling horses, O king, the earth was strewn over; and with steeds tongueless, panting, neighing, and lifeless—horses of every form, O best of men—the ground was made resplendent.

sanskrit: arjunena hataiḥ saṃkhye tathā bhārata vājibhiḥ prababhau vasudhā ghorā tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: With the horses slain by Arjuna in the encounter, O descendant of Bharata, the earth shone dreadful here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: rathair bhagnair dhvajaiś chinnaiś chatraiś ca sumahāprabhaiḥ hārair niṣkaiḥ sakeyūraiḥ śirobhiś ca sakuṇḍalaiḥ
english: With chariots shattered, banners cut down, and parasols of dazzling splendour, with necklaces and golden chains and armlets, and with heads still bearing their earrings—

sanskrit: uṣṇīṣair apaviddhaiś ca patākābhiś ca sarvaṣaḥ anukarṣaiḥ śubhai rājan yoktraiś cavyasuraśmibhiḥ saṃchannā vasudhā bhāti vasante kusumair iva
english: With turbans flung down, and pennons on every side, with shining axle-poles, O king, and with yoke-straps and reins now lifeless—the earth, so covered, shone as in springtime strewn with blossoms.

sanskrit: evam eṣa kṣayo vṛttaḥ pāṇḍūnām api bhārata kruddhe śāṃtanave bhīṣme droṇe ca rathasattame
english: Thus too did this destruction befall the Pāṇḍavas, O descendant of Bharata, when the son of Śaṃtanu, Bhīṣma, was wrathful, and Droṇa, that best of chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmni kṛpe caiva tathaiva kṛtavarmaṇi tathetareṣu kruddheṣu tāvakānām api kṣayaḥ
english: And when Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa, and likewise Kṛtavarman, and the others too were wrathful, destruction came upon your men as well.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vartamāne tathā raudre rājan vīravarakṣaye śakuniḥ saubalaḥ śrīmān pāṇḍavān samupādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: While that fierce slaughter of the best of heroes was going on, O king, the illustrious Śakuni, son of Subala, rushed upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tathaiva sātvato rājan hārdikyaḥ paravīrahā abhyadravata saṃgrāme pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: And likewise the Sātvata, the son of Hṛdika, slayer of hostile heroes, O king, charged in battle against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāmbojamukhyānāṃ nadījānāṃ ca vājinām āraṭṭānāṃ mahījānāṃ sindhujānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then with the foremost steeds of the Kāmbojas and those born of the rivers, the horses of the Āraṭṭas, those bred on the great land, and those of the Sindhu in every kind—

sanskrit: vanāyujānāṃ śubhrāṇāṃ tathā parvatavāsinām ye cāpare tittirajā javanā vātaraṃhasaḥ
english: with the gleaming horses born in Vanāyu and those that dwell in the mountains, and others, the swift partridge-coloured ones, fleet as the wind—

sanskrit: suvarṇālaṃkṛtair etair varmavadbhiḥ sukalpitaiḥ hayair vātajavair mukhyaiḥ pāṇḍavasya suto balī abhyavartata tat sainyaṃ hṛṣṭarūpaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: with these chief horses, decked in gold, armoured and well caparisoned, swift as the wind, the mighty son of the Pāṇḍava, that scorcher of foes, his form glad with eagerness, advanced upon that army.

sanskrit: arjunasyātha dāyāda irāvān nāma vīryavān sutāyāṃ nāgarājasya jātaḥ pārthena dhīmatā
english: Now Arjuna's heir, the valiant one named Irāvān, was begotten by the wise son of Pṛthā upon the daughter of the king of the Nāgas.

sanskrit: airāvatena sā dattā anapatyā mahātmanā patyau hate suparṇena kṛpaṇā dīnacetanā
english: She, childless, her husband slain by Suparṇa, piteous and forlorn of mind, had been given by the high-souled Airāvata.

sanskrit: bhāryārthaṃ tāṃ ca jagrāha pārthaḥ kāmavaśānugām evam eṣa samutpannaḥ parakṣetre 'rjunātmajaḥ
english: And the son of Pṛthā took her to wife, for she yielded to her desire; thus was this son of Arjuna born in a field not his own.

sanskrit: sa nāgaloke saṃvṛddho mātrā ca parirakṣitaḥ pitṛvyeṇa parityaktaḥ pārthadveṣād durātmanā
english: He grew up in the world of the Nāgas, sheltered by his mother, but cast off by his evil-minded uncle out of hatred for the son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: rūpavān vīryasaṃpanno guṇavān satyavikramaḥ indralokaṃ jagāmāśu śrutvā tatrārjunaṃ gatam
english: Handsome, endowed with valour, virtuous, and true in his prowess, he went swiftly to the world of Indra on hearing that Arjuna had gone there.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ pitaraṃ satyavikramam abhyavādayad avyagro vinayena kṛtāñjaliḥ irāvān asmi bhadraṃ te putraś cāhaṃ tavābhibho
english: Approaching his high-souled father of true prowess, calm and with palms joined in reverence, he saluted him: "I am Irāvān; blessings on you—I am your son, O lord."

sanskrit: mātuḥ samāgamo yaś ca tat sarvaṃ pratyavedayat tac ca sarvaṃ yathāvṛttam anusasmāra pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And he made known all that union with his mother had been; and the Pāṇḍava recalled the whole of it just as it had come to pass.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya sutaṃ cāpi so ''tmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ guṇaiḥ prītimān abhavat pārtho devarājaniveśane
english: And embracing his son, who in qualities was the very likeness of himself, the son of Pṛthā was filled with joy in the abode of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: so 'rjunena samājñapto devaloke tadā nṛpa prītipūrvaṃ mahābāhuḥ svakāryaṃ prati bhārata yuddhakāle tvayāsmākaṃ sāhyaṃ deyam iti prabho
english: Then in the world of the gods, O king, the mighty-armed one was charged by Arjuna with affection concerning his own affairs, O descendant of Bharata: "In the time of battle you must lend us your aid, O lord."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity evam uktvā ca yuddhakāla upāgataḥ kāmavarṇajavair aśvaiḥ saṃvṛto bahubhir nṛpa
english: "So be it," he said, and when the time of battle had come, he arrived, O king, surrounded by many horses of various hues and at-will swiftness.

sanskrit: te hayāḥ kāñcanāpīḍā nānāvarṇā manojavāḥ utpetuḥ sahasā rājan haṃsā iva mahodadhau
english: Those horses, with golden frontlets, of many colours and swift as thought, sprang up of a sudden, O king, like wild-geese upon the great ocean.

sanskrit: te tvadīyān samāsādya hayasaṃghān mahājavān kroḍaiḥ kroḍān abhighnanto ghoṇābhiś ca parasparam nipetuḥ sahasā rājan suvegābhihatā bhuvi
english: Closing with your swift bands of horses, striking chest against chest and muzzle against muzzle upon one another, they fell suddenly to the ground, O king, smitten by the force of their charge.

sanskrit: nipatadbhis tathā taiś ca hayasaṃghaiḥ parasparam śuśruve dāruṇaḥ śabdaḥ suparṇapatane yathā
english: And from those bands of horses falling thus upon one another, a fearsome sound was heard, as at the swooping of the great birds.

sanskrit: tathaiva ca mahārāja sametyānyonyam āhave parasparavadhaṃ ghoraṃ cakrus te hayasādinaḥ
english: And likewise, O great king, the horsemen, meeting one another in the fray, wrought a dreadful mutual slaughter.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne saṃkule tumule bhṛśam ubhayor api saṃśāntā hayasaṃghāḥ samantataḥ
english: As that turmoil raged on, exceedingly furious and confused, the bands of horses on both sides were brought to ruin on every side.

sanskrit: prakṣīṇasāyakāḥ śūrā nihatāśvāḥ śramāturāḥ vilayaṃ samanuprāptās takṣamāṇāḥ parasparam
english: The heroes, their arrows spent, their horses slain, worn out with toil, came to destruction, hewing one another down.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣīṇe hayānīke kiṃciccheṣe ca bhārata saubalasyātmajāḥ śūrā nirgatā raṇamūrdhani
english: Then, when the cavalry was depleted and but little of it remained, O descendant of Bharata, the heroic sons of Subala came forth to the forefront of the fight.

sanskrit: vāyuvegasamasparśā jave vāyusamāṃs tathā āruhya śīlasaṃpannān vayaḥsthāṃs turagottamān
english: Mounting the finest horses, whose touch was swift as the wind's rush and who in speed matched the wind, well-trained and in their prime—

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo vṛṣakaś carmavān ārjavaḥ śukaḥ ṣaḍ ete balasaṃpannā niryayur mahato balāt
english: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Vṛṣaka, Carmavān, Ārjava, and Śuka—these six, endowed with strength, sallied forth from the great host.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇāḥ śakuninā svaiś ca yodhair mahābalaiḥ saṃnaddhā yuddhakuśalā raudrarūpā mahābalāḥ
english: Though held back by Śakuni and by their own mighty warriors, these—armoured, skilled in war, terrible of aspect, and exceedingly strong—

sanskrit: tad anīkaṃ mahābāho bhittvā paramadurjayam balena mahatā yuktāḥ svargāya vijayaiṣiṇaḥ viviśus te tadā hṛṣṭā gāndhārā yuddhadurmadāḥ
english: breaking through that most unconquerable host, O mighty-armed one, joined with great force and seeking victory for the sake of heaven, those Gāndhāras, frenzied for battle, entered it then in their gladness.

sanskrit: tān praviṣṭāṃs tadā dṛṣṭvā irāvān api vīryavān abravīt samare yodhān vicitrābharaṇāyudhān
english: Seeing them so entered, the valiant Irāvān then spoke in the battle to his warriors, who bore varied ornaments and weapons:

sanskrit: yathaite dhārtarāṣṭrasya yodhāḥ sānugavāhanāḥ hanyante samare sarve tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: "Let such a course be ordained that these warriors of the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with their followers and mounts, may all be slain in the battle."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity evam uktvā te sarve yodhā irāvataḥ jaghnus te vai parānīkaṃ durjayaṃ samare paraiḥ
english: "So be it," said all those warriors of Irāvān, and they smote that hostile host, hard for foes to conquer in battle.

sanskrit: tad anīkam anīkena samare vīkṣya pātitam amṛṣyamāṇās te sarve subalasyātmajā raṇe irāvantam abhidrutya sarvataḥ paryavārayan
english: Seeing that host struck down by the host in the battle, the sons of Subala, all unable to brook it, rushed upon Irāvān and surrounded him on every side in the fight.

sanskrit: tāḍayantaḥ śitaiḥ prāsaiś codayantaḥ parasparam te śūrāḥ paryadhāvanta kurvanto mahad ākulam
english: Striking with sharp lances and urging one another on, those heroes ran about, working great confusion.

sanskrit: irāvān atha nirbhinnaḥ prāsais tīkṣṇair mahātmabhiḥ sravatā rudhireṇāktas tottrair viddha iva dvipaḥ
english: Then Irāvān, pierced by the sharp lances of those high-souled ones, was smeared with streaming blood, like an elephant goaded with the driver's hooks.

sanskrit: urasy api ca pṛṣṭhe ca pārśvayoś ca bhṛśāhataḥ eko bahubhir atyarthaṃ dhairyād rājan na vivyathe
english: Sorely struck upon the breast and the back and both flanks—one against many—yet, O king, through his steadfastness he did not waver at all.

sanskrit: irāvān atha saṃkruddhaḥ sarvāṃs tān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ mohayām āsa samare viddhvā parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: Then Irāvān, that conqueror of hostile cities, full of wrath, pierced them all with whetted arrows and bewildered them in the fight.

sanskrit: prāsān uddhṛtya sarvāṃś ca svaśarīrād ariṃdamaḥ tair eva tāḍayām āsa subalasyātmajān raṇe
english: And that subduer of foes, plucking out all the lances from his own body, smote the sons of Subala in the battle with those very weapons.

sanskrit: nikṛṣya niśitaṃ khaḍgaṃ gṛhītvā ca śarāvaram padātis tūrṇam āgacchaj jighāṃsuḥ saubalān yudhi
english: Drawing his whetted sword and taking up his shield, on foot he came swiftly forward, eager to slay the sons of Subala in the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇāḥ sarve te subalātmajāḥ bhūyaḥ krodhasamāviṣṭā irāvantam athādravan
english: Then all those sons of Subala, their spirits returned to them, once more filled with rage, rushed upon Irāvān.

sanskrit: irāvān api khaḍgena darśayan pāṇilāghavam abhyavartata tān sarvān saubalān baladarpitaḥ
english: And Irāvān too, with his sword displaying the deftness of his hand, advanced against all those sons of Subala, proud in his strength.

sanskrit: lāghavenātha carataḥ sarve te subalātmajāḥ antaraṃ nādhyagacchanta carantaḥ śīghragāminaḥ
english: As he moved with such nimbleness, all those sons of Subala, ranging about swift-footed, could find no opening in him.

sanskrit: bhūmiṣṭham atha taṃ saṃkhye saṃpradṛśya tataḥ punaḥ parivārya bhṛśaṃ sarve grahītum upacakramuḥ
english: Then, seeing him standing upon the ground in the encounter, they all once more closed about him tightly and set about to seize him.

sanskrit: athābhyāśagatānāṃ sa khaḍgenāmitrakarśanaḥ upahastāvahastābhyāṃ teṣāṃ gātrāṇy akṛntata
english: Then, of those who had drawn near, that tormentor of foes, with his sword, cut away their limbs with strokes both upward and downward.

sanskrit: āyudhāni ca sarveṣāṃ bāhūn api ca bhūṣitān apatanta nikṛttāṅgā gatā bhūmiṃ gatāsavaḥ
english: And the weapons of them all, and their arms too, though decked with ornaments, fell; their bodies cut to pieces, they sank lifeless to the ground.

sanskrit: vṛṣakas tu mahārāja bahudhā parivikṣataḥ amucyata mahāraudrāt tasmād vīrāvakartanāt
english: But Vṛṣaka, O great king, wounded in many places, escaped from that most terrible hewing-down of heroes.

sanskrit: tān sarvān patitān dṛṣṭvā bhīto duryodhanas tataḥ abhyabhāṣata saṃkruddho rākṣasaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Seeing them all fallen, Duryodhana then, alarmed and full of wrath, addressed a Rākṣasa of dreadful aspect—

sanskrit: ārśyaśṛṅgiṃ maheṣvāsaṃ māyāvinam ariṃdamam vairiṇaṃ bhīmasenasya pūrvaṃ bakavadhena vai
english: the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, a great archer, a master of illusion and a subduer of foes, enemy to Bhīmasena ever since the slaying of Baka of old.

sanskrit: paśya vīra yathā hy eṣa phalgunasya suto balī māyāvī vipriyaṃ ghoram akārṣīn me balakṣayam
english: "Behold, O hero, how this mighty son of Phalguna, a master of illusion, has done me a dire and grievous harm, the destruction of my forces."

sanskrit: tvaṃ ca kāmagamas tāta māyāstre ca viśāradaḥ kṛtavairaś ca pārthena tasmād enaṃ raṇe jahi
english: "And you, dear friend, move at will and are skilled in the weapons of illusion, and you bear enmity against the son of Pṛthā; therefore slay him in the battle."

sanskrit: bāḍham ity evam uktvā tu rākṣaso ghoradarśanaḥ prayayau siṃhanādena yatrārjunasuto yuvā
english: "So be it," said the Rākṣasa of dreadful aspect, and with a lion's roar he set forth to where the young son of Arjuna was.

sanskrit: svārūḍhair yuddhakuśalair vimalaprāsayodhibhiḥ vīraiḥ prahāribhir yuktaḥ svair anīkaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ nihantukāmaḥ samare irāvantaṃ mahābalam
english: Attended by warriors well-mounted and skilled in war, who fought with gleaming lances, by valiant smiters, and surrounded by his own ranks, he came eager to slay the mighty Irāvān in the battle.

sanskrit: irāvān api saṃkruddhas tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī hantukāmam amitraghno rākṣasaṃ pratyavārayat
english: But Irāvān too, full of wrath, swift and valiant, that slayer of foes, held off the Rākṣasa who sought to kill him.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ saṃprekṣya rākṣasaḥ sumahābalaḥ tvaramāṇas tato māyāṃ prayoktum upacakrame
english: Beholding him rushing on, the Rākṣasa of exceeding might, in haste, then set about to employ his illusion.

sanskrit: tena māyāmayāḥ kḷptā hayās tāvanta eva hi svārūḍhā rākṣasair ghoraiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇibhiḥ
english: By him were fashioned, all by illusion, horses just as many, mounted by dreadful Rākṣasas bearing pikes and spears in their hands.

sanskrit: te saṃrabdhāḥ samāgamya dvisāhasrāḥ prahāriṇaḥ acirād gamayām āsuḥ pretalokaṃ parasparam
english: Those two thousand smiters, meeting in fury, ere long sent one another to the world of the dead.
